title: Simulación de los Parámetros de Diseño y Construcción de una Aeronave Radiocontrolada
relevance: One of the few primary publications naming the UglyStik: reports a rebuilt geometry (1.56 m span, 0.59 m² wing area, 1.38 m length), control throws and a NACA 63(2)-015 wing section; uses Winfoil and AAA for design/cruise estimates.
limitations: The paper explicitly states that it did not formulate a mathematical flight-dynamics model. The coefficients are design-software estimates, not measured aircraft derivatives; geometry and model identity are not the Jensen 60.

title: Development, Analysis, and Implications of Open-Source Simulations of Remotely Piloted Aircraft
relevance: Chapter 5 documents a JSBSim Giant Big Stik model and checks it against flight-test sections; tables report geometry, mass properties, aerodynamic coefficients and control travel. The full thesis provides more implementation context than the shorter 2019 paper.
limitations: The SAA validation is fit-for-purpose and narrow: short, low-risk pitch/roll sections; takeoff and landing excluded; rudder excluded from the comparison and throttle treated as constant near 50%. The thesis reports manual gain/offset/delay adjustments and correlations of roll 0.9304 and pitch 0.60664/0.74044 on two selected intervals. Winds and different initial states limit replay agreement. This is Giant Big Stik, not Jensen Ugly Stik.

title: Identifikasi Model dari Pesawat Udara Tanpa Awak Sayap Tetap Jenis Bixler
relevance: A Bixler aircraft is identified from experimental flight data using a fourth-order longitudinal state-space model; useful as an aircraft-specific structural and instrumentation comparator.
limitations: The 12-page Indonesian-language paper reports a small experiment and uneven model prediction quality; it is not a complete six-degree-of-freedom model or a public raw-flight-log release. Interpret translated terms and reported accuracy in the context of the original text.

title: System Identification of a Nonlinear Flight Dynamics Model for a Small, Fixed-Wing UAV
relevance: Detailed flight-derived nonlinear model for a conventional tailed Bix3 trainer: 1.202 kg, 1.54 m projected span and 0.285 m² projected wing area. The thesis combines output-error fitting, flight-maneuver selection, data conditioning and VLM priors, and discusses parameter uncertainty.
limitations: No direct angle-of-attack or sideslip measurement; the integrated airspeed sensor is reported unreliable, states are reconstructed from low-cost sensors, and the calm-day flight data have limited information/noise. Flaps are omitted and the model should not be treated as a Bixler 1/2 fit or as unbounded-envelope validation.

title: Bixler 3 Flight Test Analysis
relevance: A Stanford AA241X project report gives logged Bixler 3 flight observations, including throttle-off glide segments, trajectory/altitude and estimated glide angle; it can guide qualitative performance checks and points to the distinction between flight behavior and aerodynamic-model validation.
limitations: Student project report, not peer reviewed; the observed glide path is wind-affected and the parameter estimates rely on a small set of filtered segments. No raw data archive was identified with the report. The filename in this folder says 2024 for retrieval bookkeeping, but the PDF itself is dated 2017-04-25.

title: Flight Test Instrumentation System for Small UAS System Identification
relevance: Tests an onboard system with air-data, inertial navigation, and direct control-deflection measurement on a quarter-scale PA-18 Super Cub; up to 100 Hz logging; OKID-derived linear models were checked against flight data with different input sets. Strong evidence for sensor/actuator logging needs on a conventional trainer.
limitations: The reported models are local linear state-space models around tested trim conditions, not a full nonlinear aerodynamic database. Super Cub geometry, mass and powertrain differ from the Jensen Stik.

title: A Low-cost Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Research Platform: Development, Modeling, and Advanced Control Implementation
relevance: A 6-foot conventional high-wing Telemaster study measures inertias and servo response, models the propulsion system, identifies longitudinal/lateral aerodynamic parameters from flight data using output error, and compares model responses with later validation runs.
limitations: The platform is a modified research UAV rather than an unmodified sport model; the thesis reports that OEM documentation omitted turbulence and describes flights selected for minimal disturbance. Do not transfer coefficients directly to a Stik.

title: Validation of a Small UAV Dynamic Model Using CFD and Flight Test Data
relevance: Develops a six-degree-of-freedom model from CFD and compares it with three flight-test sets; reports modal and time-history agreement alongside pitch/airspeed residuals, a useful example of explicit model discrepancy reporting.
limitations: The tested airframe is not identified as an RC hobby model in the available article information and is not geometrically comparable to the Stik. CFD-derived coefficients and mixed error levels make it method evidence rather than a source of transferable Stik derivatives.

title: Aerodynamic Modeling of the Skywalker X8 Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
relevance: Compares numerical aerodynamic tools and static wind-tunnel coefficients in a complete X8 model; useful for separating measured static terms from model-assumed damping derivatives.
limitations: X8 is a tailless flying wing, not a conventional trainer. Static tunnel measurements do not identify dynamic damping; the paper reports that its initial tunnel-fit model predicted flight acceleration poorly. This file duplicates the flying-wings branch by content hash and should be deduplicated during integration.

title: Estimation of the Lateral Aerodynamic Coefficients for Skywalker X8 Flying Wing from Real Flight-Test Data
relevance: Estimates lateral aerodynamic coefficients from real closed-loop flight-test data, addressing parameter correlation with prior information and constrained optimization and testing the estimates against additional flight data.
limitations: Flying-wing geometry and controller feedback make results specific to this airframe/model structure. Not direct evidence for a conventional tail or Jensen Stik. This file duplicates the flying-wings branch by content hash and should be deduplicated during integration.

title: Modeling of the Skywalker X8 Fixed-Wing UAV: Flight Tests and System Identification
relevance: The paper shows that an earlier static tunnel model with near-unit fit could still have negative flight acceleration fitness; it adds flight-derived damping and compares an improved model against flight data.
limitations: The X8 is a flying wing and the fitted damping/model assumptions are aircraft-specific. This file duplicates the flying-wings branch by content hash and should be deduplicated during integration.

title: Time-Domain System Identification and Validation of Small Fixed-Wing UAV Dynamics
relevance: Identifies a 44-coefficient aero-propulsive/actuator model and tests predictions against separate short flight maneuvers; reports that amplitude and wind conditions affect agreement.
limitations: Results concern the tailless 3.36 kg X8 and approximately 18 m/s flight. Wind sensitivity and model choices limit transfer to a tailed RC sport aircraft. This file duplicates the flying-wings branch by content hash and should be deduplicated during integration.

title: Skywalker X8 System Identification Flight Data (DataverseNO DOI 10.18710/U4TLYV)
relevance: Machine-readable X8 system-identification collection with training and validation maneuvers; archive inventory indicates 17 approximately ten-second maneuver records and MAT files suitable for independent model comparison.
limitations: Campaign data collected in 2023 on a tailless flying wing; the paper describes strong NW wind including a vertical component, so wind and air-data reconstruction must be accounted for. This archive duplicates the flying-wings branch by content hash and should be deduplicated during integration.

title: Modeling and Identification of a Small Fixed-Wing UAV Using Estimated Aerodynamic Angles
relevance: Provides a complete nominal X8 model using estimated aerodynamic angles and published flight validation; reports aircraft dimensions/mass, a 44-coefficient structure and explicit limits away from trim.
limitations: The authors identify wind and air-angle estimation error, decoupled longitudinal/lateral modeling, poor excitation of slow spiral behavior, and decreasing accuracy away from trim/at negative angle of attack. The aircraft is a tailless wing. This file duplicates the flying-wings branch by content hash and should be deduplicated during integration.

title: System Identification for Small, Low-Cost, Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aircraft
access: existing-local-reference; not duplicated by this collection
relevance: Frequency-domain identification from designed flight experiments, with separate time-domain validation for the 25e; strong comparison source for methods and modes.
limitations: The 25e is a different electric model and size from the Jensen Stik; its coefficients are not transferable without scaling and configuration evidence.

title: Test Platforms for Model-Based Flight Research
access: existing-local-reference; not duplicated by this collection
relevance: Reports Ultra Stick platform properties, inertia measurement, flight-identified lateral matrices and modes; provides full dissertation context.
limitations: Model-specific configuration and identification conditions must match; the thesis includes several platforms, so use the 25e sections/tables rather than treating all values as one aircraft.

title: Synthetic Air Data Estimation: A Case Study of Model-Aided Estimation
access: existing-local-reference; not duplicated by this collection
relevance: Includes a model of the 8.338 kg Ultra Stick 120 and published linear model matrices useful for a trainer-class cross-check.
limitations: The dissertation focuses on synthetic air data; model coefficients belong to this larger testbed and are not Stik planform validation.

title: Development of a Low-Cost Sub-Scale Aircraft for Flight Research: The FASER Project
access: existing-local-reference; not duplicated by this collection
relevance: Describes the NASA FASER platform, high-quality flight instrumentation, operations and wind-tunnel model; establishes testbed provenance and measurement practice.
limitations: FASER is a modified, research-instrumented Ultra Stick 120. It is a methods/platform paper, not an Ugly Stik dynamics measurement.

title: Forced Oscillation Wind Tunnel Testing for FASER Flight Research Aircraft
access: existing-local-reference; not duplicated by this collection
relevance: Measures FASER roll/yaw damping as rate, angle of attack and reduced frequency vary; supports scrutiny of analytically supplied dynamic derivatives.
limitations: Wind-tunnel model is a research-modified Ultra Stick 120; numerical values are mostly figure-derived, and rotating-flow results are not direct Stik flight data.

title: Giant Big Stik R/C UAV Computer Model Development in JSBSim for Sense and Avoid Applications
access: Official article HTML accessible; direct publisher PDF request returned HTTP 403; no third-party mirror retained.
relevance: Peer-reviewed article version of the Giant Big Stik JSBSim case study; its online full text describes adjustments against flight data and a purpose-limited sense-and-avoid validation.
limitations: Same project as the local 2020 thesis, not an independent aircraft experiment. The short validation remains limited to selected conventional maneuvers; use the thesis for detailed caveats.

title: Modeling and Flight Simulation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Enhanced with Fine Tuning
access: Publisher landing page and abstract accessible; full text paywalled; no paywall bypass attempted.
relevance: The publisher abstract identifies a COTS Tiger-Trainer platform, a six-degree-of-freedom simulation, and longitudinal tuning from flight-test data; useful conventional high-wing comparison if the full text is obtained legally.
limitations: Only publisher abstract/metadata was accessible in this pass; full article access requires subscription or author copy. No coefficients or detailed validation results were relied upon here.

title: System Identification and Multi-Objective Longitudinal Control Law Design for a Small Fixed-Wing UAV
access: DOI/metadata lead only; no verified primary full text downloaded. Third-party reposts were not retained.
relevance: Bibliographic lead for frequency-domain identification of a 12% Cessna 182 model and subsequent flight testing of longitudinal control laws; potentially useful if an official free paper copy is located.
limitations: The original paper was not obtained from an official freely accessible repository in this pass; metadata only is recorded here. No results or parameters are used as evidence.

title: Cub Crafters CC11-100 Sport Cub S2 UAVDB flight-test CSV archive
access: Full 53-CSV ZIP downloaded; ZIP member CRCs pass. UAVDB FAQ says its data are free to download and use with citation; no standard data license was identified.
relevance: A 26%-scale Cub Crafters CC11-100 Sport Cub S2 collection with recorded responses for control inputs, descents, phugoids, stalls and six named spin conditions. The metadata describes IMU, GPS, airspeed, position, motor, battery and control-surface channels, so the logs can support time-response, trim, stall-entry and spin-trend comparisons.
limitations: Related RC airframe, not the Jensen Ugly Stik 60. The CSV archive combines measured, filtered and derived channels; it is not the original DAQ binary. The archive header defines units but not a single uniform rate. An inspected high-rate spin file has repeated Time values, so do not assume a fixed-step grid from its filename.

title: Flight & Ground Testing Data Set for Subscale GA Aircraft: 26%-scale Cub Crafters CC11-100 Sport Cub S2
access: Downloaded from the UAVDB author/institutional site; PDF signature and text verified.
relevance: Primary description of the flight and ground data package behind the local UAVDB Cub archive. It documents the RC test aircraft, instrumentation, flight-test plan and examples of measured aircraft responses.
limitations: Paper plots and reported observations are not a substitute for the archived time series. It describes the Cub testbed, not an Ugly Stik, and the available CSV archive contains transformed/filtered fields alongside measured channels.

title: UAVDB Great Planes Avistar Elite maneuver-data record
access: Metadata-only; official data page currently lists no files.
relevance: An especially close RC trainer lead: the Avistar Elite page describes 400 Hz data acquisition, GPS/IMU, pitot-static airspeed, PWM control commands and propulsion signals. The site indicates that a planned maneuver-data release would be directly useful for trim, control response and stall comparisons.
limitations: The current official data page says “Coming Soon!!”; no flight logs were downloadable when checked. The associated 2020 paper says its pitot-static probe was planned for installation, so measured airspeed must be verified against the exact data release/configuration.

title: Flight & Ground Testing Data Set for an Unmanned Aircraft: Great Planes Avistar Elite
access: Downloaded from the UAVDB site; PDF signature, metadata and searchable text verified.
relevance: Primary flight and ground test study of a conventional high-wing RC trainer (3.70 kg gross, 1.59 m span). The paper describes 400 Hz acquisition, repeated trim/control-response maneuvers, nominal 20 m/s flight, and stall tests at standard and heavier mass; it reports that the standard-mass airplane mushed/slipped while a 250 g heavier configuration showed a clearer stall.
limitations: The published paper contains plots and aggregate results rather than downloadable telemetry. Its 2019 instrumentation section says the pitot-static probe would be installed later; do not treat airspeed in this paper’s flight histories as a measured pitot channel without checking the relevant file. UAVDB now lists a pitot probe but still has no current maneuver-data download.

title: Defining Handling Qualities of Unmanned Aerial Systems: Phase II Final Report
access: Full NASA NTRS report downloaded; NTRS marks distribution Public and Public Use Permitted.
relevance: A substantial measured-flight anchor for the 1.92 m UMN Ultra Stick 120 RC-derived UAS. The report documents actual flight-test response data at 23 m/s cruise and 17 m/s low-speed/50%-flap condition, nominal and aft-CG configurations, added feedback delays, and multi-sine, frequency-sweep, doublet and pulse excitations; Appendix C contains flight-test plots.
limitations: The report’s plots and model comparisons are not an open raw telemetry log. The approach condition was flown level at lower speed with flaps, not as a real landing approach. Transfer to an Ugly Stik requires matching geometry, mass, CG, control and propulsion configuration.

title: System Identification for Small, Low-Cost, Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aircraft
access: Reuses the exact existing local paper; no duplicate copy made.
relevance: Flight-identifies an RC Ultra Stick 25e (1.959 kg, 1.27 m span) using frequency-response fits and validates linear/nonlinear models against time histories. It reports 50 Hz synchronized IMU and command data, angular-rate/acceleration noise, and a disciplined route from chirp excitation to identified model.
limitations: Related RC airframe, not the project aircraft; article does not provide the raw time-series archive. Identified linear model/plots should be compared only at matched trim, control and normalization conventions.

title: Test Platforms for Model-Based Flight Research
access: Reuses the exact existing local thesis; no duplicate copy made.
relevance: Detailed UMN research-aircraft and avionics account with flight-test design and Ultra Stick 25e identification/validation results. It helps interpret the companion 2012 paper and distinguish flight-equipped 25e/120 vehicles from the wind-tunnel-only Ultra Stick Mini.
limitations: Thesis is a measurement/method report, not a downloadable public flight-log set. Results are from UMN configurations and should not be copied as Ugly Stik-specific coefficients.

title: Synthetic Air Data Estimation: A Case Study of Model-Aided Estimation
access: Reuses the exact existing local thesis; no duplicate copy made.
relevance: Documents actual Ultra Stick 120 sensor/flight-test evidence useful for comparing air-data estimators and deciding which simulator states are directly measured versus reconstructed. The instrumentation includes inertial/navigation data and air-data measurements such as pitot and vanes.
limitations: Primary focus is air-data estimation rather than aircraft aerodynamic identification; no raw log archive is bundled. Estimated alpha/beta/airspeed states are not ground truth and should not be conflated with independent sensor measurements.

title: Development of a Low-Cost Sub-Scale Aircraft for Flight Research: The FASER Project
access: Reuses exact existing NASA-hosted PDF; no duplicate copy made.
relevance: A first-party design and instrumentation account for the NASA FASER research aircraft based on an RC Ultra Stick 120. It describes 50 Hz IMU/INS and GPS, control-surface potentiometers, wingtip alpha/beta vanes, velocity probes, battery telemetry, 400 Hz oversampling for analog channels, flight operations and data compatibility.
limitations: The paper reports instrumentation and selected plots, not a downloadable raw log set. Historical avionics and signal conditioning differ from the simulator’s sensor model; raw sensor values required systematic corrections.

title: Forced Oscillation Wind Tunnel Testing for FASER Flight Research Aircraft
access: Reuses exact existing NASA-hosted PDF; no duplicate copy made.
relevance: Measured FASER roll/yaw damping across alpha, sideslip, oscillation amplitude, nondimensional rate and reduced frequency, with control-deflection cases. This gives physical dynamic-aerodynamic evidence for a related RC airframe and documents comparison with UMN Ultra Stick flight-rate data.
limitations: Wind-tunnel forced oscillations are not free-flight telemetry. The report’s coefficients depend on motion/test setup and should not be treated as a direct measured simulator trajectory.

title: Rotary Balance Wind Tunnel Testing for the FASER Flight Research Aircraft
access: Reuses exact existing NASA-hosted PDF; no duplicate copy made.
relevance: Combines 20-ft vertical spin-tunnel rotary-balance data (alpha 0–50°, beta −5–10°, nondimensional spin rate −0.5 to 0.5) with an actual FASER flight-spin observation. Especially useful for testing whether a model can represent spin-entry tendencies and the mismatch between steady-spin prediction and a dynamic flight event.
limitations: Rotary-balance results are tunnel measurements. The paper reports only one flight-spin example and the IMU roll-rate gyro saturated during it; spin rates are partly estimated from video/other channels and the predicted equilibrium spin was not found.

title: System Identification for a Small, Rudderless, Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aircraft
access: Reuses exact existing UMN-hosted PDF; no duplicate copy made.
relevance: Reports flight experiments and model validation for a 1.28 kg, 0.97 m-span rudderless fixed-wing aircraft, including elevator/aileron-equivalent chirp inputs and modal estimates. Useful as a cross-check on roll, Dutch-roll and control-response scales when a conventional four-control RC model is unavailable.
limitations: Rudderless elevon aircraft is not a conventional trainer or Ugly Stik; few control effectors make its identifiable derivatives configuration-specific. Raw telemetry is not bundled.

title: AirLab Failure and Anomaly (ALFA) fixed-wing flight-data corpus
access: Official CMU dataset page links a public KiltHub deposit. Figshare API metadata lists separate processed/raw/DataFlash/telemetry ZIPs and CC BY 4.0; archives not locally downloaded.
relevance: Real outdoor Carbon-Z T-28 flight records cover nominal and failed-engine/elevator/aileron/rudder conditions. Official documentation describes 47 processed flight sequences, raw ROS bags, Pixhawk DataFlash and companion-computer telemetry; synchronized commanded/measured attitude, velocity and airspeed are typically 20–25 Hz, with IMU about 10 Hz, GPS about 4–5 Hz and fault labels at 5 Hz.
limitations: Fault/anomaly data focus, not systematic aerodynamic identification, stall or spin. It has a 2 m modified Carbon-Z airframe and autopilot loops; use measured-versus-commanded channels carefully. Full collection is 1.7 GB compressed, so not mirrored under the local-size cap.

title: ALFA: A Dataset for UAV Fault and Anomaly Detection
access: Downloaded arXiv author preprint; PDF signature/text verified.
relevance: Primary paper identifies the testbed as a modified 2 m Carbon-Z T-28 with single electric engine, ailerons/flaperons/elevator/rudder, Pixhawk, pitot, GPS and Jetson TX2. It provides the channel/topic inventory, sample rates, fault types and dataset structure needed before using the ALFA corpus.
limitations: Only a portion of the corpus is devoted to nominal aircraft behavior; faults are injected by modified autopilot logic and safety pilot retains recovery authority. It is not an open-loop aerodynamic coefficient database.

title: Fixed-Wing UAS Telemetry Benchmark (IDF_DS): 240 Flights for ML and Intelligent Trajectory Optimization
access: Public Zenodo v1.0 record, CC BY 4.0; two downloadable archives are listed (about 2.1 GB and 580.8 MB), not locally mirrored.
relevance: Broad open corpus of 240 outdoor waypoint-guided fixed-wing missions across SpeedyBee/INAV and Pixhawk 6X/PX4+Jetson architectures. The repository and article describe synchronized IMU, GNSS, barometer, pitot where fitted, flight modes, actuator commands/states and electrical metrics; these logs can ground estimator, control-loop, sensor-noise and trajectory comparisons.
limitations: Mission/autonomy data are not dedicated high-alpha, stall or spin tests and aircraft/firmware configuration matters. Two ZIPs total about 2.7 GB; no representative archive was mirrored under the 80 MB local cap. Dataset documentation must be followed for channel-specific rates, units, missing/uncalibrated pitot cases and timing.

title: An open benchmark dataset for machine learning and intelligent trajectory optimization in fixed-wing unmanned aerial systems
access: Full text publicly readable in PMC; PDF download endpoint was not usable in this retrieval session, so no local PDF copy.
relevance: Primary Scientific Data article documents the IDF-DS aircraft, acquisition platforms, 240 missions, over 32 flight-hours, 160 telemetry channels, directory layout and reuse conditions. It is the source for interpreting the large external corpus rather than a source of separately mirrored samples.
limitations: Open-access paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, distinct from the dataset’s CC BY 4.0. The article body has one DOI digit typo; use the bibliography/Zenodo canonical record 10.5281/zenodo.16992976. No raw rows were downloaded.

title: Flight-Test System Identification of Leading-Edge Rime-Ice Effects on a Small Fixed-Wing UAV: dataset ReadMe
access: Downloaded official bundled README and read it in full; see the separate clean and iced sample entries for inspected time-series rows.

limitations: The README describes processing but does not substitute for raw flight logs. Its CC BY 4.0 statement conflicts with the Dataverse record metadata showing CC0 1.0; license scope remains unresolved.

This entry covers only the clean CSV; see the separately identified paired iced sample.

Author-derived aero coefficients and battery drag power depend on the original specific propeller/powertrain model and must not be treated as model-independent measurements. Repository page shows CC0 1.0 while bundled README says CC BY 4.0; resolve license scope with depositor before reuse beyond research. title: FliTePlat UAV flight-test dataset supporting Southampton theses and drag-curve study
access: Public catalog record; dataset page reports CC BY, but direct binary requests were blocked by the host in this environment.
relevance: Official Southampton record lists three measured flight logs supporting the FliTePlat small fixed-wing study. The aircraft’s instrument suite includes dual Pixhawk recorders, conventional Pitot-static and Kiel/static air-data systems, GNSS, motor voltage/current and optical RPM; the paper analyzes 45 glides and 55 slow-down maneuvers.

These records emphasize performance/drag identification rather than general aerobatic dynamics. Do not unpickle files until a trusted, safe read path is established.

title: Experimental Evaluation of the Drag Curves of Small Fixed Wing UAVs
access: Publisher full text and DOI metadata are publicly readable; no PDF copied locally in this collection. The separate Southampton dataset record lists the associated raw logs.
relevance: A measurement-oriented small-aircraft paper compares wind-tunnel and flight-derived lift/drag curves with multiple methods. It documents FliTePlat’s pitot/Kiel air-data systems, redundant Pixhawk recorders, optical RPM and electrical logging, and repeated glide/slow-down tests; useful for identifying measurement bias and repeatability limits.
limitations: Not RC sport/aerobatic validation and not a raw-log release itself. Flight methods show gust, altitude, propeller-position, battery/powertrain-model and maneuver-repeatability errors; the paper warns that some assumptions bias drag estimates.

title: Flexible Diana 2 Scaled Glider UAV - Aeroelastic Flight Test Measurements
access: Public 4TU.ResearchData deposit, DOI 10.4121/0c3fcef0-5b63-480c-ae40-3ff726c657e9; not mirrored in this batch.

The repository describes 5-hole-probe airspeed/alpha/beta, GPS, Pixhawk attitude/commands, 12 distributed IMUs, 21 strain gauges, control-surface encoders and calibration artifacts; useful to stress sensor/structural coupling and command-versus-deflection comparisons.

title: Spin Aerodynamic Modeling for a Fixed-Wing Aircraft Using Flight Data
access: Citation and abstract accessible through the author laboratory page and DOI; no paper or log copy mirrored.
relevance: Primary AIAA/author-page study develops a nonlinear coupled spin aerodynamic model from actual spinning fixed-wing flight data using orthogonal phase-optimized multisine excitation and independent validation flights. The author page emphasizes why a nominal level-flight model fails to represent stable oscillatory spin behavior.
limitations: No raw flight logs or unrestricted official PDF were found in this pass. The accessible author publication entry supplies the abstract/citation but not a complete measurement-channel/time-rate inventory; treat reported model findings as paper evidence rather than a downloadable benchmark.

title: Aerodynamic modeling of the Skywalker X8 Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
access: Downloaded public author copy; valid PDF signature and title/text verified.
relevance: A whole-airframe X8 case study with measured static wind-tunnel force and moment coefficients and a simulation-oriented aerodynamic model.
limitations: Static loads were measured, but the final stability derivatives were supplied by XFLR5 rather than measured in the tunnel; match the paper's geometry, reference axes, and test conditions.

title: Estimation of the Lateral Aerodynamic Coefficients for Skywalker X8 Flying Wing from Real Flight-Test Data
access: Downloaded from the publisher platform; valid PDF signature and article title/text verified.
relevance: Direct X8 lateral stability and control derivative estimates from flight data, with comparison to analytical estimates and additional flight-test validation.
limitations: The flights used closed-loop PID control; the paper explicitly addresses collinearity with priors and constrained estimation, so the estimates are method-dependent and not raw open-loop response.

title: Systems Identification, Flight Performance, and Control of a Fixed-Wing UAV in Icing Conditions
access: Downloaded public author copy; valid PDF signature and title/abstract verified.
relevance: Detailed small-flying-wing icing methodology and software flight-performance/control analysis that complements the later flight-test work.
limitations: The abstract describes static and unsteady derivatives from CFD and software simulation; it explicitly says flight-test validation remains future work. Its reduced-frequency model has stated frequency/amplitude and separation limits.

title: Stability of a Flying Wing UAV in Icing Conditions (author-corrected version)
access: Downloaded public author-corrected PDF; valid PDF signature and correction notice/title verified.

title: Modeling of the Skywalker X8 Fixed-Wing UAV: Flight Tests and System Identification
access: Downloaded public author copy; valid PDF signature and title/abstract verified.
relevance: Combines static X8 tunnel coefficients with flight-identified damping and critiques validation against tunnel fit alone.
limitations: Reuses the prior X8 tunnel dataset for much of the static model and uses flight data for damping; it is a particular campaign and modeling structure, not a universal coefficient set.

title: Time-Domain System Identification and Validation of Small Fixed-Wing UAV Dynamics
access: Downloaded public author postprint; valid PDF signature and title/abstract verified.
relevance: Builds a six-degree-of-freedom X8 model from tunnel propulsion work and flight experiments, with model predictions for separate 10-second maneuvers near 18 m/s.
limitations: The model is identified and validated for the reported maneuvers and estimated airdata; weather, state estimation, propulsion and servo models contribute uncertainty. This is not a high-angle-of-attack or raw-data-only benchmark.

title: System identification campaign - Skywalker X8 UAV
access: Downloaded public DataverseNO dataset ZIP; ZIP CRC check passed and README/file structure inspected.
relevance: CC0 archive with 17 X8 maneuvers (13 training, four validation), original MAT and interoperable CSV series, including accelerations, rates, states, control commands, and estimated airdata.

Alpha/beta depend on estimated wind and airspeed; tests had strong north-west wind with a vertical component. Embedded README gives DOI `10.18710/U4TL`, unlike the canonical Dataverse DOI `10.18710/U4TLYV`.

title: Modeling and identification of a small fixed-wing UAV using estimated aerodynamic angles
